strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: milp-direct-minimax
Replacement scope: Replace the bisection loop (the `for _ in range(15)` block and the repeated `milp` calls) inside `compute_model_placement`, keeping the greedy seed placement as warm-start/fallback.
Compute budget: One or two `scipy.optimize.milp` calls per instance with time_limit 2–5 s each; expected evaluation time roughly equal to or below the current 15-call bisection (~2.6 s).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent solves a sequence of feasibility MILPs via bisection, wasting solver restarts and leaving up to 2^-15-relative slack on T. Instead solve a single MILP with an explicit epigraph variable T ≥ 0 and per-GPU linearized constraints Σ_i (r_i + T·s_i)·x[i,g] ≤ T·GPU_MEM_SIZE. This is bilinear in (T, x), so linearize exactly by fixing T only once: iterate T via a secant/outer loop on the *analytic* reduced problem — or more simply, since T·s_i·x is the only bilinear term, use the exact reformulation: constraint per GPU becomes Σ r_i x[i,g] ≤ T·(GPU_MEM_SIZE − Σ s_i x[i,g]), which is linear in x for fixed T. Run a *golden-section* (not bisection) on T with 25 iterations and warm-start each MILP from the previous feasible assignment as an incumbent hint via `options={"mip_rel_gap":0}` and reduced time limits (0.2 s after the first call), since feasibility MILPs warm-start trivially by keeping the last feasible x as a hint. The new degree of freedom vs. the incumbent: (1) 25 vs 15 refinement steps closing the T interval by ~10^6× instead of 3×10^4×, (2) warm-started feasibility solves rather than cold ones, (3) a final polishing step that, given the optimal T*, re-solves a min-Σ(max_g load slack) MILP to spread load evenly among GPUs achieving T*, often lowering the true max KVPR below the bisection's granularity floor. Hard constraints preserved: assignment-exactly-once and memory constraints are kept verbatim; the greedy placement is returned whenever any MILP call fails or the polished solution is infeasible/worse.

strategies.title: [lexicographic-hillclimb] Deterministic lexicographic hill-climb with pair-swap
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lexicographic-hillclimb
Replacement scope: Replace the final "accept MILP result if better" phase with a post-processing hill-climb applied to whichever placement (greedy or MILP) is currently best, inside `compute_model_placement`.
Compute budget: At most 2000 neighborhood evaluations per instance (single sweep passes over all (model, gpu) moves and all model-pair swaps between the two highest-KVPR GPUs, repeated until no improving move, capped at ~20 sweeps); pure Python/numpy, expected added time < 0.5 s per instance.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's MILP linearizes KVPR as Σ(r_i + T·s_i)x ≤ T·MEM, which is exact only at the bisection's fixed T; the true objective (load/(MEM−size)) is nonlinear, so the MILP-optimal assignment can be strictly suboptimal in true max KVPR. A hill-climb on the *true* objective closes this gap. Use a lexicographic objective: minimize (max KVPR, second-max KVPR, third-max KVPR, …) computed exactly, so moves that don't reduce the max but flatten the runner-up GPUs are accepted, enabling later moves that do reduce the max. Neighborhood: (a) move any single model to any GPU where it fits, (b) swap any two models between two GPUs if both fit afterwards. Accept the best improving move per sweep (steepest descent, fully deterministic — no RNG, avoiding the earlier annealing family's crash-prone random choice from empty sequences). Invariant: every candidate move is checked for memory feasibility (free_mem[g] − size > 0, or == 0 with zero resulting load) before evaluation, so the hard capacity constraint is never violated; the incumbent placement is returned if no move improves.
Expected-gain check: The MILP's linearization error at fixed T is a calculable gap the incumbent cannot close by construction, while the hill-climb optimizes the exact KVPR formula; a falsifiable threshold is any instance where the MILP assignment's true max KVPR exceeds the linearized bound, which the polish strictly reduces, yielding combined_score > 26.256.

strategies.title: [auction-dual-ascent] Auction-style GPU price equilibrium
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: auction-dual-ascent
Replacement scope: Replace the MILP-bisection refinement block inside `compute_model_placement`; greedy seeds remain the incumbent and fallback.
Compute budget: at most 200 auction rounds, each round a single O(n·gpu_num) pass over models; expected evaluation time negligible (< 0.05 s per instance), reducing the 2.6 s runtime while possibly improving max_kvpr.
Gain mechanism: Introduce per-GPU prices p_g (dual variables) that the incumbent lacks entirely. Initialize p_g = 0. Each round: every model i "bids" for the GPU g minimizing c(i,g) = r_i/(M − S_g − s_i) + p_g among memory-feasible GPUs (c = ∞ if it does not fit); assign each model to its best GPU. Then update prices by a subgradient step on the max-KVPR: for the GPU g* with the highest KVPR, raise p_{g*} by ε·(kvpr_{g*} − median kvpr) (ε = 0.05, clipped to ≥ 0), and lower the price of the GPU with the lowest KVPR by the same total (prices are shift-invariant, so renormalize mean price to 0 every 10 rounds). This pushes load off the hot GPU gradually — a continuous rebalancing direction, unlike the incumbent's discrete all-or-nothing bisection. Track the best feasible assignment seen (memory feasibility is checked explicitly at assignment time, so validity is guaranteed); after 200 rounds or 30 rounds without improvement, return the best. If no round beats the greedy incumbent, return the incumbent.
Plan: pure numpy, no external solver; maintain S_g, L_g incrementally; recompute KVPR vector once per round; guard division by zero (free memory ≤ 0 with positive load ⇒ kvpr = ∞ ⇒ that GPU is always the hot one and gets maximal price pressure). The new degree of freedom is the price field on GPUs, which produces a smooth escape direction from imbalanced greedy local optima that pairwise moves in the spent hill-climb families only reach by luck.

strategies.title: [cross-entropy-sampling] Cross-entropy distribution over assignments
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: cross-entropy-sampling
Replacement scope: Replace the MILP-bisection refinement block inside `compute_model_placement`; keep greedy seeds as incumbent and feasibility-repair source.
Compute budget: at most 60 CE iterations × 30 samples = 1800 assignment evaluations per instance, each O(n) with incremental per-GPU KVPR recomputation; expected evaluation time < 1 s per instance.
Gain mechanism: Maintain a probability matrix P[i,g] (softmax over GPUs, initialized peaked at the greedy incumbent's assignment with temperature giving ~0.7 mass on the incumbent choice). Each iteration: sample 30 full assignments (each model independently drawn from its row of P, fixed RNG seed 0 for determinism); repair each sample for memory feasibility by a deterministic pass — any model on an overfull GPU moves to a feasible GPU with minimal resulting KVPR, infeasible samples are discarded; evaluate true max KVPR of survivors; take the elite fraction (best 25%) and update P by maximum-likelihood toward the elite assignments with learning rate 0.7, plus a small uniform smoothing of 0.02 to avoid collapse. Hard validity: every candidate is memory-checked and repaired before evaluation; the incumbent fallback guarantees no regression.

Mechanism family: agglomerative-merge
Replacement scope: Replace the greedy seed
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: agglomerative-merge
Replacement scope: Replace the greedy seed phase (`try_order`/`try_reserve` and the `orderings` list) that feeds the MILP bisection; keep the MILP bisection phase unchanged as the incumbent fallback and incumbent upper bound.
Compute budget: At most O(n²) merge evaluations per run, single run per instance (no multistart). Expected evaluation-time effect: negligible added time (<0.3 s) versus the existing MILP budget; total stays near current 2.6 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's greedy seeds are strictly sequential — each model is placed before later models are seen, so a large low-rate model placed early can never be split from the small high-rate models it should share a GPU with. Agglomerative merging gives a globally-informed constructive seed: start with each model as its own cluster; repeatedly merge the pair of clusters (i,j) whose merged KVPR (r_i+r_j)/(160 − s_i − s_j) is smallest among pairs that fit in one GPU (s_i+s_j < 80), until exactly gpu_num clusters remain; assign clusters to GPUs (all identical, any bijection works). If a merge is infeasible for all pairs before reaching gpu_num clusters, fall back to the incumbent greedy seed. This produces structurally different seeds than any ordering-based greedy — it pairs complementary (low-rate/large-memory) models first, which is exactly the tension the evaluator guide identifies. The merged seed then either beats the greedy incumbent directly or tightens T_hi for the existing MILP bisection, which can only improve the final result since the bisection already keeps the best assignment found.
Hard validity: every model is in exactly one cluster, each cluster's total model_size < 80, so the assignment is feasible; if merging cannot reach gpu_num clusters the incumbent greedy result is returned unchanged.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is non-sequential complementary pairing of models, which no ordering-based greedy in the incumbent can realize; if it finds any instance where the greedy seed's max KVPR exceeds the merge seed's, the MILP bisection's returned max KVPR strictly decreases on that instance, so the falsifiable threshold is: average 1/avg_kvpr across the benchmark strictly above the current 26.256.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: gp-relax-slsqp
Replacement scope: Replace the entire MILP bisection phase (the `import numpy/scipy.optimize.milp` block after `kvpr_of`) with a continuous relaxation solved by scipy SLSQP; keep the greedy seed phase as incumbent fallback.
Compute budget: One SLSQP solve (≤200 iterations, n·gpu_num variables) plus one deterministic rounding pass; expected added time <0.5 s per instance, replacing the 15-round MILP bisection so total time should drop.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's MILP bisection linearizes the fractional KVPR via a threshold T and is limited to 15 coarse feasibility probes with 0.5 s each — it can miss the optimum between probes and frequently times out. Instead solve the epigraph form directly and continuously: variables x[i,g] ∈ [0,1] (assignment fractions) plus T; minimize T subject to Σ_g x[i,g] = 1 for each model i, Σ_i s_i·x[i,g] ≤ 80 for each GPU g, and the exact nonlinear constraint Σ_i (r_i + T·s_i)·x[i,g] − T·80 ≤ 0 for each g. This constraint set is exactly equivalent to KVPR_g ≤ T when x is binary, and the relaxation is smooth (quadratic in x·T), so SLSQP with analytic gradients converges to the fractional optimum — a lower bound on the true optimum that no bisection probe attains. Rounding: sort fractional cells x[i,g] by value descending; assign each model to its highest-fraction GPU if memory permits, else the feasible GPU with smallest current KVPR; verify every model placed (fractions near 1 for all i in practice since the constraint matrix is totally-unimodular-like in structure for fixed T). Compare rounded result's true max KVPR against the greedy incumbent and keep the better. Hard validity: rounding only places a model on a GPU whose remaining memory ≥ model_size, and a final check that all n models are placed; otherwise return the greedy incumbent placement.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the exact fractional optimum of the epigraph formulation (the incumbent's bisection only samples 15 thresholds and its linearization is identical only at the optimum), so on any instance where rounding is integral or near-integral the max KVPR strictly drops below the incumbent's T_hi; falsifiable threshold: average 1/avg_kvpr > 26.256 with execution time ≤ ~3 s.

Mechanism family: quota-apportionment
Replacement scope: Add as an additional seed generator feeding the existing best-of comparison (the `best = ...; for order in orderings` block), replacing nothing else; the MILP phase and greedy seeds remain as fallback.
Compute budget: One deterministic pass, O(n log n + n·gpu_num); no iterations, no multistart; adds <50 ms.

A quota method balances the numerator directly: compute the ideal per-GPU rate quota Q = (Σ_i r_i)/gpu_num where r_i = req_rate/slo. Process models in descending r_i; maintain per-GPU "rate debt" d_g = Q − Σ r on g; assign each model to the GPU with the largest debt d_g among those with free memory ≥ s_i, breaking ties by most free memory. Then run one repair sweep: while some GPU exceeds its quota and another is under, move the model minimizing the donor's KVPR increase on the receiver (respecting memory) from the max-KVPR GPU to the min-KVPR GPU, up to n sweeps. This is the classical largest-remainder apportionment adapted with memory feasibility — a construction with no sequential-order dependence and an explicit balance target the incumbent lacks; its output is a genuinely different basin for the MILP bisection's T_hi. Hard validity: every assignment checks free memory ≥ model_size before placing; if any model cannot be placed the seed is discarded and the incumbent placement is returned.

strategies.title: [column-generation] Subset-pool ILP: generate good GPU "bins" and select the bes
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: column-generation
Replacement scope: Replace the entire `compute_model_placement` body (both greedy seeds and the MILP-bisection phase) with a two-stage pipeline: (A) candidate-bin generation, (B) exact set-partition ILP over the generated bins.
Compute budget: At most ~3000 candidate bins generated deterministically (greedy fills from multiple sort orders with randomized-restricted-choice-free deterministic tie-breaks); one `scipy.optimize.milp` call with a 2-second time limit; fallback to the incumbent greedy if anything fails. Expected runtime ≤ 3 s per instance, comparable to current 2.6 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent optimizes model→GPU assignments one model at a time (greedy) or via a bisection that only checks feasibility at a fixed T with no objective gradient between feasible points. Column generation changes the search representation: each decision variable is an entire *subset* of models on one GPU, pre-screened so that only bins with low KVPR (load/(mem−size)) and feasible memory enter the pool. The final ILP is a set-partitioning problem: choose exactly gpu_num bins covering each model exactly once, minimizing the maximum bin KVPR (min-max linearized by an auxiliary variable Z with constraints bin_kvpr·y_b ≤ Z). This lets the solver combine complementary high-rate/small-model with low-rate/large-model pairs globally — a combination the sequential greedy provably cannot reach because its per-step KVPR criterion rejects temporarily unbalanced bins.
Plan: (1) Enumerate bins by greedy fill: for each of ~8 deterministic orderings (r/s desc, size desc, r desc, and mixed keys), repeatedly open a bin and add the model that minimizes the bin's KVPR while fitting memory; also generate bins from the incumbent greedy placement and single-model perturbations of it (move one model between GPUs, keep the two affected bins as candidates). (2) Prune: drop bins whose KVPR exceeds the incumbent's max KVPR (they can never help the optimum). (3) Solve the set-partition min-max ILP with `milp` (binary y_b per bin, continuous Z; constraints: per-model coverage = 1, Σy_b = gpu_num, kvpr_b·y_b ≤ Z). strategies.title: [admm-dual-decomposition] Consensus ADMM over per-GPU subproblems with KVPR-line
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: admm-dual-decomposition
Replacement scope: Replace the MILP-bisection block (everything after the greedy `best` is chosen) with an ADMM refinement loop that keeps the greedy placement as fallback and initial point.
Compute budget: ≤ 300 ADMM iterations, each iteration O(n·gpu_num) pure numpy (no solver calls); expected added runtime < 0.5 s per instance.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's bisection treats the problem as pure feasibility and gets no gradient signal between feasible thresholds; ADMM instead continuously relaxes the binary assignment into [0,1] with a per-GPU local subproblem that has a closed-form solution, then enforces consensus (each model fully on one GPU) via augmented Lagrangian penalties, and rounds the fractional solution deterministically. This gives a different escape direction: fractional mass can drift gradually toward the balanced solution across iterations, crossing valleys the discrete moves in the incumbent's construction cannot.

(2) Per-iteration: for each GPU g, solve the local subproblem min over x_g of Σ_i r_i x_ig + penalty terms, subject to Σ_i s_i x_ig ≤ MEM — this is a fractional knapsack with a simple ratio-sort closed form (sort models by r_i/(s_i+λ) and fill greedily); the global coupling is the per-model row-sum = 1 constraint handled by dual variables u_ig updated with step ρ. (3) Every 25 iterations, round X (assign each model to its max-x GPU, repairing memory violations by moving the smallest-r/s violators to feasible GPUs) and evaluate the true max KVPR; keep the best rounded solution. (4) Return the best of {ADMM-rounded, greedy incumbent}. Validity: the greedy fallback plus repair-on-rounding guarantee a valid, memory-feasible partition always.

strategies.title: [ratio-transfer-balancing] Closed-form worst-to-best GPU transfer loop with lexi
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ratio-transfer-balancing
Replacement scope: Replace the MILP-bisection refinement block (after the greedy `best` is selected) with a deterministic transfer-and-swap balancing loop; the greedy placement remains the fallback.
Compute budget: ≤ 200 improving transfers/swaps per instance, each evaluated in O(1) with incremental KVPR updates (no solver calls); expected added runtime < 0.1 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's greedy phase never revisits a placement after construction, and its bisection phase only accepts whole new assignments from an opaque solver. This loop adds a *directed* local mechanism the incumbent lacks: repeatedly identify the worst-KVPR GPU, and for every model on it compute the exact closed-form post-move KVPR of both affected GPUs for every destination, plus the analogous closed-form swap with models on other GPUs; accept the single best strictly-improving move, where "improving" means lexicographic (max KVPR decreases, or max ties and second-max decreases). Gain mechanism: The incumbent bisection solves one global feasibility MIP whose linearization is weak when memory is tight; fix-and-optimize instead freezes all models except those on the two currently worst GPUs and re-solves a tiny exact MIP over just those two GPUs (all subsets of their union assigned to one of the two GPUs, minimizing the max of the two resulting KVPRs). Concretely: pick the GPU pair (worst, second-worst or worst, best), extract their models, solve the two-GPU assignment MIP with variables x[i,g] for those models only, memory constraints per GPU, and objective minimizing an auxiliary variable T with constraints sum_i (r_i + T*s_i)*x[i,g] <= T*GPU_MEM_SIZE (T free, x binary, each model assigned once). If the solved max KVPR of the pair is strictly lower than before, commit; iterate over pairs by descending KVPR until no pair improves or budget exhausts. Hard validity: memory constraints are in every subproblem, every model stays assigned, and any solver failure keeps the previous feasible incumbent.
Expected-gain check: each committed pair step strictly reduces that pair's max KVPR without increasing any other GPU, so the instance max KVPR is monotonically non-increasing and strictly decreases whenever the greedy/bisection incumbent is pair-locally suboptimal — a falsifiable threshold is any instance where the current score's max KVPR exceeds the two-GPU optimum, which the tiny MIPs certify exactly.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: recursive-load-bisection
Replacement scope: Replace the ordering-seed list and greedy assignment phase of `compute_model_placement` with a recursive bisection constructor; keep the incumbent's existing MILP bisection phase unchanged downstream as a polisher/fallback.
Compute budget: the constructor is O(n log n) per level with at most ceil(log2(gpu_num)) levels and a small DP per split (subset-sum over model sizes capped at 2^k with k<=20, else greedy split); negligible time added; downstream MILP budget unchanged.
Gain mechanism: All current seeds are sequential greedy orderings — they commit models one at a time and can never reconsider the global load split. Recursive bisection instead splits the model set into gpu_num groups simultaneously: at each step, partition the current model multiset into two halves whose weighted loads (r = req_rate/slo) and memory sums are as equal as possible (DP on rounded load with memory-feasibility side constraint: each half's total size must leave enough room for its share of the remaining capacity, i.e., half_size <= half_count*GPU_MEM_SIZE where half_count is the number of GPUs each side will feed). Recurse until each group feeds exactly one GPU; a group whose size exceeds GPU_MEM_SIZE triggers a repair step that swaps its largest model with the smallest model of the least-full sibling group. This produces a geometrically different seed — balanced in both numerator (load) and denominator (memory) simultaneously — which the order-based greedy cannot represent, and the downstream MILP bisection then polishes from a better upper bound T_hi, tightening its feasible interval. Hard validity: memory capacity is enforced at every leaf with repair, and the incumbent placement is kept if the new seed's max KVPR is not better.
Expected-gain check: the new seed's max KVPR is computed explicitly and only replaces the incumbent when strictly lower, so the returned objective is min(incumbent, bisection seed) — the gain is realized exactly on instances where balanced simultaneous partitioning beats sequential greedy, a falsifiable threshold measurable per instance before the MILP phase runs.

strategies.title: [homotopy-objective-ramping] Continuation from load-balancing to KVPR minimax
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: homotopy-objective-ramping
Replacement scope: Replace the greedy ordering/seed phase (the `orderings` list and `try_order`/`try_reserve` selection) plus keep the incumbent MILP-bisection phase as a final polish; the ramping heuristic replaces how the incumbent seed is constructed.
Compute budget: one pass of ~50 ramp steps × n model-move evaluations per instance (O(50·n·gpu_num) delta evaluations), well under the current MILP time; expected evaluation time similar to or below current 2.6 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent greedy commits each model irrevocably based on instantaneous KVPR only; it cannot trade a temporarily worse KVPR for a better final configuration. The homotopy starts from an easy near-optimal objective — minimize max per-GPU load Σr (a plain makespan, solvable well by LPT greedy) — and continuously morphs the per-GPU cost from load to true KVPR, c = (1−λ)·load/free + λ·load/(free), re-running local moves at each λ so the assignment tracks the solution path. This exposes a degree of freedom (the order in which memory vs load tension is resolved) that any single-objective greedy or single MILP bisection start cannot explore, and it produces a different (often better) incumbent fed into the existing MILP bisection, which can only tighten around its upper bound.
Plan: (1) Build assignment by LPT on r = req_rate/slo (largest first, least resulting load, memory-feasible). (2) For λ = 0, 0.02, …, 1: compute blended cost c_g(λ) = (load_g + ε)/(free_g) with blend (1−λ)·(load_g/norm) + λ·kvpr_g normalized so scales match; repeatedly scan all single-model moves (model → different GPU, memory-feasible) and accept the move minimizing max blended cost; stop the inner loop when no move improves. (3) Feed the λ=1 result as the new incumbent into the existing MILP bisection (unchanged), which now starts from a tighter T_hi. (4) Hard constraints preserved: every move is checked against GPU_MEM_SIZE before acceptance; all models always assigned; final result compared against the current greedy incumbent and the better one returned, so score can only improve or stay equal.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the solution path from load-makespan optimum to KVPR minimax, which neither the greedy seeds nor a single MILP bisection start can traverse; a falsifiable threshold is max-KVPR strictly below the incumbent's 25.256 average on at least one benchmark instance, with the accept-only-if-better guard guaranteeing no regression.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: farthest-point-clustering
Replacement scope: Replace the seed-construction phase (`orderings`, `try_order`, `try_reserve` seeds) with a Gonzalez-style farthest-point clustering of models into gpu_num groups; keep the MILP bisection phase and the incumbent fallback intact.
Compute budget: O(n²) distance computations once per instance (n is small, tens of models), plus one greedy repair pass; negligible added time (<0.1 s).
Gain mechanism: All incumbent seeds are sequential greedy insertions ordered by a scalar key; they can never produce a globally "spread" partition because each decision is myopic. Farthest-point clustering builds the partition top-down: pick the model with the largest combined footprint (e.g., max of r + α·size), then iteratively assign the still-unassigned model that is farthest (in a scaled 2-D metric over (model_size, req_rate/slo)) from every existing group's centroid, opening a new GPU group when available and otherwise joining the group whose post-join KVPR is lowest subject to memory. This geometric spread directly attacks the evaluator-noted tension (high-rate models must avoid memory-heavy GPUs): distance in the 2-D metric forces separation of large-size and high-rate models across GPUs, which no scalar sort key can guarantee.
Plan: (1) Scale s and r to comparable ranges (divide by max). (2) Seed group 0 with the model maximizing r_scaled + s_scaled. (3) Repeat gpu_num−1 times: among unassigned models, take the one maximizing min-distance to existing group centroids; open a new group with it (centroid = the model itself). (4) Assign each remaining model (farthest-first order) to the feasible group (memory check: group size sum + model_size < GPU_MEM_SIZE) minimizing resulting group KVPR; if none feasible, put it on the GPU with most free memory after a repair pass that evicts the smallest-KVPR-impact model to another feasible GPU. (5) Evaluate max KVPR; compare with greedy incumbent and MILP result; return the best. Hard constraints: memory checked at every join; eviction repair only moves models to feasible GPUs; every model ends assigned exactly once.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a top-down geometric partition in the joint (size, rate) space — a topology the scalar-ordering greedy provably cannot produce (its first model choice fixes a chain of myopic decisions) — with falsifiable threshold: average inverse-max-KVPR above 26.256 on the benchmark, guarded by returning the incumbent if clustering does not beat it.

strategies.title: [cooperative-coevolution] Per-GPU subpopulation co-optimization of assignment ma
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: cooperative-coevolution
Replacement scope: Replace the post-greedy local-improvement role (i.e., inserted between the greedy seed selection and the MILP bisection, replacing nothing else); MILP bisection stays as final polish with the coevolution output as its warm incumbent.
Compute budget: ≤ 3 full cycles × (gpu_num subproblems × 30 candidate reassignments each), each candidate evaluated in O(n); total ≤ ~90·gpu_num·n operations, bounded well under 1 s per instance.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's improvement mechanisms (greedy seeds, MILP bisection, single-swap hill climbs tried in spent families) all optimize the assignment as one flat object. Cooperative coevolution decomposes it by GPU: for each GPU g in turn, treat the set of models currently on g as an exchangeable subsystem — enumerate reassignments of that GPU's models to any other GPU (and pull-ins of single models from other GPUs into g), score each subsystem configuration by the resulting global max KVPR, keep the best, then move to the next GPU. Cycling through GPUs lets a good configuration on GPU 1 unlock moves on GPU 2 that were previously infeasible or unattractive — a coordinated multi-GPU escape direction that pairwise swap/move neighborhoods (spent: tabu-search-swap, ejection-chain, lexicographic-hillclimb) cannot reach, because those only ever touch one or two models at a time while this relocates an entire GPU's contents.
Plan: (1) Start from the best greedy seed placement. (2) For up to 3 cycles: for each GPU g, build candidate moves: (a) every model on g moved to every other feasible GPU individually; (b) all models on g redistributed by a small greedy pass over other GPUs; (c) each single model from another GPU pulled into g if memory allows. Evaluate global max KVPR after each candidate; apply the best improving one immediately (first-improvement within the subproblem). (3) Stop a cycle early if no GPU subproblem improves. (4) Pass the result to the existing MILP bisection as warm incumbent; return the best of {greedy, coevolved, MILP}. Hard constraints: every candidate move is memory-checked before evaluation; infeasible candidates skipped; assignment validity invariant maintained throughout; incumbent fallback guarantees no score regression.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is whole-GPU subsystem reconfiguration (relocating all of one GPU's models in a coordinated pass), which the incumbent's flat greedy and the spent flat/m pairwise neighborhoods structurally cannot express; falsifiable threshold: average inverse-max-KVPR strictly above 26.256, with the accept-only-if-better guard ensuring the floor is the current score.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: waterfilling-dual-ascent
Replacement scope: Replace the MILP refinement phase (everything after the greedy `placement` is chosen) with a deterministic dual-ascent/waterfilling reassignment loop; greedy seeds remain the fallback.

The incumbent's local-search attempts (hillclimb, ejection chains, annealing) all used generic pairwise swap neighborhoods with scalar max-KVPR acceptance, which plateaus on flat moves; lexicographic acceptance on the full sorted vector plus exact marginal ranking escapes the plateau where the max is tied across GPUs — the exact situation the minimax objective creates at optimality-adjacent points. It also considers single-model transfers only (not swaps), a different neighborhood contact topology than the spent swap-based families.
Plan: (1) Compute per-GPU (L_g, F_g) from the current placement. (2) Loop: identify the set of worst GPUs (within 1e-12 of max KVPR); for each model on a worst GPU, compute exact post-move KVPR of source and every feasible destination (F_h ≥ s_h... memory check F_h − s_i > 0 or == 0 with zero load); rank candidates by lexicographic improvement of the sorted KVPR vector; apply the best improving move; repeat until no improvement or 500 evaluations. (3) Never accept a move that leaves memory violated or a GPU with zero free memory and positive load. (4) Return the refined placement; the exact-phase result is untouched if no move improves.
